problem: Win the market quickly before rivals.
title: Webvan expands rapidly across cities and goes bankrupt in 2001
context: Webvan raised large sums, including an IPO, to deliver groceries ordered online from its own warehouses.
decision_made: Build large automated warehouses and expand toward 26 cities.
action_taken: Spent heavily on infrastructure ahead of demand; filed for Chapter 11 in July 2001.
observed_outcome: The company ceased operating after about three years. Reports put money raised at over $800 million and cash burn at more than $1.2 billion in two years. Former officials said delivery density was the core failure.
lessons: Expanding faster than demand density can support can destroy a logistics business; later firms expanded slowly in dense areas.
limitations: Totals differ by source. A $375 million IPO figure was not confirmed, so it is not included. Wikipedia-based details were excluded.

claims.claim_text: Webvan built large warehouses and aimed to expand to 26 cities by 2001.
Former Amazon and Webvan officials said Amazon learned to expand slowly and focus on delivery density from Webvan's collapse.
